title: Lumen Infosec questionnaire responses and evidence digest
content:
Purpose
This doc is the working response bundle for Lumen's Infosec questionnaire (initial POC phase). Goal is to provide short-form answers to their standard controls questions, link to primary evidence artifacts, and list outstanding items before we hand off to Sales/Eng for contract review. This is an iterative Drive working doc — expect edits.

Executive summary
- POC context: Lumen is evaluating Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private (VPC) for a regulated deployment. They requested questionnaire responses plus an evidence packet demonstrating encryption, network isolation, and change-control practices.
- Scope for this packet: security controls for pod-level inference runtime, key management, network topology for private deployments, logging/audit trail, and onboarding checklist for SOC2-relevant items.
- Current status: Core answers drafted, evidence snapshots captured for Dedicated POC (region: us-west-2), follow-ups required on HSM integration timelines and formal pen-test report.

Questionnaire: short answers + evidence pointers
Q1. How is customer data isolated in a Private/VPC deployment?
A1. For Private (customer-managed VPC), we deploy the Redwood control plane in the customer's VPC when requested or use a private connectivity model (AWS PrivateLink) to reach customer resources. Serving instances run in dedicated subnets with security groups that restrict inbound traffic to specified app/ingress endpoints. KV cache and model artifacts are stored on EBS volumes encrypted at-rest. Evidence: 
- evidence/lumen/vpc-network-architecture-diagram-2025-11-10.png (diagram)
- s3://redwood-evidence/lumen/poc-2025/network-config.json (Terraform state snapshot)

Q2. What encryption-at-rest and key management controls are in place?
A2. All customer data volumes and model artifacts are encrypted with AWS KMS keys. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS keys; for Hosted, we use Redwood-managed CMKs with access restricted to KMS principals used by the runtime. HSM-backed key wrapping available via AWS CloudHSM for on-prem requests. Evidence: 
- kms-key-ids.txt (contains key aliases used during POC)
- evidence/lumen/kms-policy-snippet.txt (IAM policy extract)
- cloudhsm-integration-notes-2025-12-02.md (HSM vendor config notes)

Q3. How do you protect inference request data in transit?
A3. TLS 1.2+ enforced on all endpoints. Mutual TLS (mTLS) available for Private control-plane connections on request. For Dedicated customers we can enable mTLS for internal service-to-service traffic. Evidence: 
- tls-cipher-report-2025-11-20.pdf (scanner output)
- config/mtls-enabled-example.yaml (sample config used for the POC)

Q4. What logging and audit capabilities exist?
A4. Audit logs capture request metadata (non-content metadata by default for hosted), API keys, auth events, and operator actions. For Private/Dedicated we can stream full audit logs to customer S3 or to their SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch subscription filters. Log retention policies are configurable. Evidence: 
- audit-log-snapshot-2025-12-01.json.gz (redacted request metadata for POC)
- evidence/lumen/log-streaming-setup.md (setup steps we ran during POC)

Q5. How are model versions and code changes controlled?
A5. Model artifacts are versioned in an internal artifact registry with immutable object IDs. Deployments are controlled by GitOps (Terraform + deployment manifests in repo). Rollouts support canary/A-B; each rollout is recorded in the console and exportable as a trace for audits. Evidence: 
- infra-repo-tag: v2025-11-lumen-poc (Git tag)
- github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/commit/eb32a1 (sample commit)
- rollout-trace-lumen-canary-2025-12-06.json (trace export)

Evidence index (what’s included in the packet)
1) network-architecture-diagram-2025-11-10.png — annotated VPC/subnet/security-group layout for POC
2) kms-key-ids.txt — aliases and ARNs used for EBS and S3 encryption during the POC (customer-managed key configured)
3) audit-log-snapshot-2025-12-01.json.gz — redacted, contains auth/metadata entries (PII/content redacted, hashes present)
4) tls-cipher-report-2025-11-20.pdf — automated scan results showing TLS configuration
5) cloudhsm-integration-notes-2025-12-02.md — high-level HSM wrapping approach and vendor notes
6) deployment-manifests-lumen-poc.tar.gz — manifests used for the POC cluster (sha256 listed in README)
7) infra-git-tag-v2025-11-lumen-poc.txt — pointer to Git tag for traceability
8) change-control-log-2025-11-30.csv — operator approvals/rollback events during POC
9) pen-test-request-ticket-JIRA-PT-88.txt — our internal request to schedule a pen test (pen test report pending)

Notes on redaction and data handling
- Content: For customer privacy and security we do not include raw inference outputs in evidence packages. The audit snapshot contains only non-user-content request metadata and hashed request IDs. Full content logs can be provided only under an approved DPA and with additional isolation controls.

Open items / follow-ups (owners + ETA)
1) Pen-test report (owner: Ethan Brooks) — request scheduled with external vendor, ETA 2026-01-28. We currently only have the request ticket in the packet.
2) Formal HSM configuration verification (owner: Marina Liu) — confirm wrap-key rotation policy with customer SRE; ETA 2026-01-15.
3) mTLS certificate exchange sample (owner: Tomasz Kowalski) — produce a minimal cert-exchange doc and example curl commands for Lumen; ETA 2025-12-20 (in practice we completed a test, still need one-pager).
4) SOC2 mapping spreadsheet (owner: Aisha Patel) — map questionnaire items to SOC2 controls, add to packet; ETA 2026-01-05.

Risk flags raised during POC
- Customer asked for guaranteed zero-data-retention mode for hosted API during evaluation; engineering confirmed Hosted API cannot meet that exact guarantee today due to shared cache behavior. Workaround: Dedicated/Private deployments can configure KV/cache eviction policies and disable cross-request caching for their tenancy. (Owner: Eng - Platform)
- Customer compliance team requested evidence of quarterly vulnerability scanning with CVE triage. We have scanning reports but need to assemble CVE triage evidence and timelines. (Owner: SRE)

Action checklist (immediate)
- [ ] Compile pen-test scoping statement and include ticket export in evidence packet (Ethan)
- [ ] Export sanitized audit logs to the S3 evidence bucket and add manifest (Aisha)
- [ ] Produce one-page mTLS setup and sample cert exchange (Tomasz)
- [ ] Confirm KMS CMK rotation policy and provide rotation log extract (Marina)

Packaging instructions for handoff to Sales/Customer
1) Create an evidence.zip containing the nine indexed artifacts above. 2) Include README.txt that describes redactions and how to request additional artifacts (DPA link). 3) Provide a short summary cover email template (below) and a secure link (pre-signed S3 URL valid 7 days).
Suggested cover email (short)
Hi Lumen team — attached is the evidence bundle for the POC. Included: network diagram, KMS policy extracts, sanitized logs, deployment manifests, and current change-control logs. Pending: external penetration test report; expected by 2026-01-28. Let us know if you need deeper artifacts under DPA or want an on-site evidence review.

Appendix: Useful command snippets used for evidence collection
- Export specific CloudWatch log group (redacted): aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /redwood/poc/lumen --start-time 1635724800000 --end-time 1635811200000 --query 'events[?contains(message, `AUTH`)]' > audit-log-snapshot.json
- Sample KMS policy check: aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/redwood-lumen-poc | jq .
- Terraform state export (sanitized): terraform state pull > sanitized.tfstate.json && jq 'del(.resources[].instances[].attributes.private_ip)' sanitized.tfstate.json > network-config.json

Reviewer notes / evidence trust model
- All artifacts at s3://redwood-evidence/lumen/poc-2025/ are read-only and access-limited to the security-and-compliance role and product-ops. Pre-signed URLs are generated per request and logged.
- This doc is the canonical working source for Q&A; the packaged evidence is versioned by timestamp. Please mark anything added to the bundle in the change-control-log CSV and update the README.

History / change log
- 2025-11-18: Initial draft created (Aisha)
- 2025-11-20: Added TLS scan and network diagram (Tomasz)
- 2025-11-30: Included deployment manifests and change-control log export (Marina)
- 2025-12-02: CloudHSM integration notes added (Marina)
- 2026-01-10: Pen-test ticket and audit snapshot included; marking doc as in_review (Aisha)

Questions for legal/sales before external delivery
- Can we share sanitized audit snapshots without a signed DPA? (Legal)
- Are we authorized to show CloudHSM integration screenshots that include vendor hostnames? (Security)

Contact
For questions about this packet contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.example.com) or Security Slack: #sec-lumen-poc
